newsitem.title: USA: FBI to make public bomb letters, seek help.
newsitem.headline: FBI to make public bomb letters, seek help.

text.p: The FBI plans to make public Monday copies of two letters that may show a link between bomb attacks on an abortion clinic and a gay nightclub earlier this year in Atlanta, an FBI spokesman said.
In releasing the letters at an Atlanta news conference, the Federal Bureau of Investigation will appeal for help in tracking down the bombers.
"There's some connection," an FBI spokesman in Washington, Edwin Cogswell, said of similarities between the letters turned up by forensic investigators.
No one was killed in the abortion clinic bombing in January nor in the nightclub bombing a month later, but the blasts injured a combined total of at least 12 people.
Sources close to the investigations said last week that bomb components from the attacks were identical.

In another sign that a serial bomber may be on the loose, the sources said shrapnel from last July's Centennial Olympic Park bombing in Atlanta originated in the same foundry as that used in the other two bombs.
One investigator said authorities believed the culprits may be an extremist cell influenced by a violent rightwing millenialist theology.
An anonymous letter purported to be from an anti-abortion group called the Army of God claimed responsibility for the abortion clinic and nightclub bombings.
A total of five bombs exploded in Atlanta between last July and February.
